mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate level, as a proxy for monetary policy stance, consistently signals positive equity returns due to its inverse relationship with the risk-free rate and its role in shaping market expectations of future rate cuts. This signal is always active and does not require threshold conditions.
failure_condition: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0%, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which increases the discount rate for equity valuation and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases when FEDFUNDS > 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate and CPIAUCSL both rise over the past month, it signals a hawkish monetary policy response to inflation, which increases the discount rate and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.0% and CPIAUCSL monthly change > 0.0%
failure_condition: The interaction signal (FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both rising) fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (defined by annualized CPIAUCSL change > 2.0%), the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day forward returns due to the market's anticipation of aggressive monetary policy tightening.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases when CPIAUCSL annualized change > 2.0%.

mechanism_narrative: The level of housing starts (HOUST) serves as a leading indicator of economic activity, and its positive trend consistently signals positive equity returns due to improved consumer confidence and business investment. This signal is always active and does not require threshold conditions.
failure_condition: When HOUST is below 1400.0, the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A labor market unemployment rate below 4.0% signals a tight labor market, which increases the risk of inflation and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to heightened market volatility and policy tightening expectations.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases when UNRATE < 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: When employment growth (PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) both rise over the past month, it signals a strong economy that may trigger aggressive monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS change > 0.0% and HOUST change > 0.0% over the past month
failure_condition: The interaction signal (PAYEMS and HOUST both rising) fails to produce negative returns in more than 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In strong industrial production regimes (defined by INDPRO > 105.0), the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns due to improved business confidence and robust economic growth, which supports corporate earnings and equity valuations.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of cases when INDPRO > 105.0.
